venue.name: Ocean River Sports - Victoria Harbour Paddle Shack
venue.description: Ocean River Sports is a Victoria kayak and paddle sports outfitter that has been in business since 1981. Its Victoria Harbour Paddle Shack is on the water at 450 Swift Street, below Craft Beer Market at the bottom of Swift Street. From that dock it runs guided kayak and stand up paddleboard tours of the harbour and rents kayaks, paddleboards and waterbikes by the hour. It also arranges custom paddling trips for larger groups, and lists school groups and summer camps among the groups it takes.

facility_notes.bus_parking: There is very limited parking at the bottom of Swift Street. City paid parking is available in any spot indicated by a blue ParkVictoria numbered pole. There's a paid lot at the top of Swift Street at 500 Store that's less than a 5 minute walk from the dock.

venue.price_year_or_season: A 20 percent off tours and 30 percent off rentals promotion was advertised for September 1st to September 7th.

programs.name: Downtown Harbour Kayak Tour
programs.description: A guided kayak tour of Victoria's downtown harbour, leaving from the dock at 450 Swift Street. It runs daily year round at 1:30 PM, takes about 2.5 hours and is off the water by 4:00 PM. The published prices are $99 for an adult and $59 for a child aged 10 to 12. Their own page adds that families with children are better off booking a private tour.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle a kayak out from the dock with a guide for about two and a half hours, following the waterfront and looking out for wildlife along the way.
programs.our_note: Two and a half hours in a kayak is a long stretch for young children, and their page steers families with children towards a private tour instead. The only child price shown starts at age 10, so ask what they would do with a younger group before you count on this one.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing is published about washrooms, changing space or somewhere to eat at the dock, and they describe parking at the bottom of Swift Street as very limited. Both are worth a call before you bring a group.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $59 price is published for children aged 10 to 12. No price is shown for anyone younger.

programs.name: Sunset Kayak Harbour Tour
programs.description: A guided evening kayak tour from the downtown dock, running daily from April to September. The start time changes with the sunset and the tour takes about 2.5 hours. The published prices are $115 for an adult and $69 for a child aged 10 to 12. As with the afternoon tour, their page recommends a private tour for families with children.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle through the harbour with a guide in the evening, passing the city landmarks while the guide talks about Victoria's history.
programs.our_note: This one is on the water as the light goes, which rules it out for most young groups. If you want it with older children, get them to pin down the actual start time for your date, because it moves with the sunset.
programs.practical_summary: Start times are not listed anywhere, so you cannot plan a pick up from the site alone. Washrooms, changing space and anywhere to eat are not mentioned either.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $69 price is published for children aged 10 to 12. No price is shown for anyone younger.

programs.name: Stand-up Paddle Board Tour
programs.description: A guided stand up paddleboard tour that starts by teaching you to paddle a board and then explores the harbour, with the guides pointing out seals, eagles, seaplanes and the landmarks along the waterfront. The published prices are $99 for an adult and $59 for a child aged 10 to 12. No length or start time is published for this one.
programs.what_children_do: Learn to stand up and paddle a board, then follow the guide around the harbour, watching for seals, eagles and seaplanes.
programs.our_note: Standing on a board asks more of a child than sitting in a kayak, and neither the length of the tour nor a youngest age is published. Ask about both before you consider it for a group.
programs.practical_summary: The price is published but the length, the start times and the months it runs are not. Nothing is said about washrooms or dry clothes afterwards, and everybody should expect to get wet.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $59 price is published for children aged 10 to 12. No price is shown for anyone younger.
programs.evidence: The perfect combination: learn to SUP while exploring Victoria's stunning harbour.

programs.name: Private guided paddle
programs.description: A private 2.5 hour guided tour for a party of 2 to 12 people, at a time arranged with you. This is the option their tour pages point families with children towards. No price is published for it.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle with a guide who is looking after your group only, on a route and at a time worked out with you beforehand.
programs.our_note: This is the option their own pages send families with children to, so it is the one to ask about first. Email them your group size and the ages you actually have, because no price is published and they quote it case by case.
programs.practical_summary: The length and the group size limit are published, the price is not. Nothing is stated about washrooms or a place to eat at the dock, so ask when you enquire.
programs.evidence: We offer private 2.5 hour tours that fit your schedule! For parties of 2 to 12.

programs.name: School and group paddling trip
programs.description: For groups larger than 12, Ocean River will arrange a paddling experience with a custom length, custom start time and custom content, and names school groups and summer camps as examples. It can run from the downtown dock or from their Oak Bay location. Prices are not published and depend on group size and length, and they invite you to ask about their education and non-profit rates.
programs.what_children_do: Paddle as a group with guides, on a route and for a length of time worked out with the school in advance.
programs.our_note: This is the one to ask about for a class. Send them the group size, the ages and the date in one email, and ask about the education rate at the same time, because nothing is priced on the site.
programs.practical_summary: Everything here is arranged by email, including the price and the time on the water. Washrooms, a lunch spot and coach parking near the dock are not covered anywhere on the site, so put those in the same email.
programs.evidence: For groups larger than 12, we can arrange paddling experiences with custom lengths, custom start times, and custom content.

gaps: No minimum age is published for the harbour tours. The only child price covers ages 10 to 12 and there is no price or policy for anyone younger, so a daycare group has to ask outright whether children under 10 can go on the water at all.

Their instruction page says the Paddle Canada courses and clinics have no age restrictions but that participants must be physically able to do all the on water and safety activities. That statement is about the courses, not about the harbour tours.
No price at all is published for private tours or for group trips larger than 12. Both are quoted case by case, and education and non-profit rates are only mentioned, not listed.
Nothing is published about washrooms, changing rooms, an indoor space or anywhere to eat at the Swift Street dock.
Opening hours for the Paddle Shack are not on the site. Every page sends you to their Google listing instead.
No wet weather alternative is described for the tours. The only weather statement on the site is about the courses.
No adult to child ratio is given for group trips, and there is nothing about whether accompanying adults pay.
Minimum booking notice for a group trip is not stated.
Coach or bus parking is not mentioned. The site says only that parking at the bottom of Swift Street is very limited and lists paid lots and parkades five to ten minutes away.
The coordinates come from the map link for the downtown location on their contact page rather than from a published latitude and longitude.
The Open Graph image on every page is the Ocean River wordmark rather than a photograph, so the hero here is the dock photo from their contact page instead.

Rental prices are quoted per boat per hour rather than per person, so rentals are not recorded as a program with a group price. For reference the page lists a single kayak at $50 for 2 hours and a paddleboard at $30 for 1 hour.
Whether the tour price includes tax is not stated.

values: Rentals are now closed until Spring.
conflicts.note: Two of their pages disagree about whether boat rentals at the downtown dock are running. One says rentals are available from the 1st of May onwards, another says they are closed until spring, and the home page was advertising a discount on rentals. Worth settling on the phone before you plan around a rental.
